solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reform voters to be tried

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaign to change the electoral system is about to be put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' looks like a political noun, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange VOTERS into STROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made an effort or attempted something.

clue.text: This helps chart cycling crime

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so letters from the front travel round to the back

parts.note: arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A tool that helps map out patterns in bicycle theft.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first two letters of ARSON round to the end and you get SONAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses sound pulses to measure water depth and map the seabed, so ships use it to make charts.

clue.text: Perhaps nuclear to some, God's beginning to drop

definitions.note: an adjective describing the kind of thing the answer names

indicators.note: the opening letter falls further down the word, so the order of the letters changes

parts.note: the Creator is a name for God

explanation.surface: Some people think the nuclear option means God's influence is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the C at the top of CREATOR drops three places lower, giving REACTOR. 'Perhaps' marks nuclear as one example of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the best-known kind, so nuclear is a typical description of a reactor.

clue.text: Central Park outwardly nasty as experienced by others

indicators.note: something on the outside wraps around whatever lies within it

parts.note: vicious means nasty or cruel

indicators.note: what is central sits in the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Central Park in New York is unpleasant on the outside, as other people have found.
explanation.walkthrough: Central Park looks like the New York landmark, but it means the middle of PARK; VICIOUS opens up to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious feelings are lived through someone else's experience rather than one's own.

clue.text: Stay a while and feel part of the gang

parts.note: to stay somewhere is to be there
a while is a long time

explanation.surface: Hang around with a group for a bit and you start to feel included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay a while' is read as two words run together: BE + LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to be accepted as a member of a group and feel at home in it.

clue.text: Wood finally wore thin

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: last letter of the word
bony means very thin, all skin and bone

explanation.surface: A piece of timber eventually wore down to almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wore thin' reads as a phrase, but 'wore' only lends its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard, dark timber from tropical trees, used for piano keys and carving.

clue.text: Done with friend returning to share space

parts.note: over means finished, done

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Having finished, a returning friend moves in to share a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done with friend' sounds like ending a friendship; here 'with' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Things overlap when they partly cover each other and occupy some of the same area.

clue.text: Countryside award for martial arts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the protected open land ringing a British city
second meaning: a coloured grade in judo or karate

explanation.surface: A rural prize handed out for judo or karate.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is the protected rural ring around a town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both protected rural land and an intermediate rank awarded in many fighting disciplines.

clue.text: Fashionable and lavish from a very young age

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
fancy means elaborate or lavish

explanation.surface: Someone stylish and extravagant since childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of a lifelong show-off, but splits into two adjectives followed by the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest stage of life, babyhood and early childhood.

clue.text: Obstacle race starts in 38 degrees? Always

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it

parts.note: 38 degrees Celsius is a raised body temperature

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An obstacle race beginning in sweltering heat, as it always does.
explanation.walkthrough: 38 degrees looks like the weather, but the question mark signals body temperature: normal is about 37°C, so 38 is a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever means for all time, at every moment, without end.

clue.text: Broadcasts three-wheeler attack

parts.note: a station airs a programme when it broadcasts it
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: News bulletins report an assault involving a tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The break between the pieces does not match the break in the answer: the S of the first piece starts the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: An air strike is a military assault made by aircraft bombing or firing on a target.

clue.text: 9 originally ignored by oddly formal brotherhood

indicators.note: the original, opening letter is left out and passed over
oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word
the answer to 9 means always, and so does this word

explanation.surface: A formal society that ignores the beginning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is a cross-reference: take a synonym of that answer, FOREVER, rather than the answer itself, then drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraternity is a brotherhood, a society of men linked by a common interest or bond.

clue.text: Country where money exchanges hands

indicators.note: swapping one hand for the other trades right for left, a one-letter switch

parts.note: the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: A nation where cash passes from person to person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchanges hands' sounds like trading, but it means swap R (right) for L (left) in RAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Land is used to mean a nation or realm, as in 'the land of the free'.

clue.text: Body temperature, roughly

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: An approximate reading of someone's body temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body temperature' reads as one phrase, but 'Body' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human frame, without the head and limbs.

clue.text: Item covering ill-considered defeat

indicators.note: a cover goes round whatever it shields, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a thing is an item
rash means hasty and ill-considered

explanation.surface: A news story covering up a careless loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item covering' sounds like a press report on something, but 'covering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a heavy, one-sided loss in a game or contest.

clue.text: Discarded all clothing that's pinstriped

parts.note: the tail of the word, read as a word in its own right
the opening letter of the word, which the following 'in' places inside the rest

explanation.surface: Someone who took off every stitch, including a pinstripe suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pinstriped' as P-IN-STRIPED: the letter P goes inside STRIPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stripped is to have removed every garment and been left naked.

clue.text: Nonsense part below a grim layout

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is below comes after the other piece
a layout is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor dismisses a role buried at the bottom of a bleak page design.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks are listed in answer order; in the clue the part comes first but sits below the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, confused and pointless procedure or story, so it means nonsense.

clue.text: One kneels for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a poser is someone who poses, as a model does

explanation.surface: Someone gets down on one knee to strike a pose for a model.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little scene: the traditional marriage proposal is made kneeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A man asking for a woman's hand traditionally goes down on one knee, so the suitor is the kneeler.

clue.text: Police officer in shoddy finale of action film spoiler?

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it

parts.note: poor means shoddy, of low quality
PC is a police constable

indicators.note: a finale is the ending, so only the last letter counts

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cop in a dreadful ending to a blockbuster that ruins the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film spoiler' usually means revealing the plot; the question mark signals the snack whose rustling and crunching spoils a cinema visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The snack munched noisily by other cinemagoers can ruin the movie for everyone nearby.

clue.text: Soldiers like Goliath

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
a soldier ant, the warrior caste of an ant colony

explanation.surface: Troops who resemble the biblical warrior Goliath.
explanation.walkthrough: The one plural word supplies two soldiers. The definition winks at the setter, who calls himself Goliath.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath, the Philistine felled by David, was enormous, so something resembling him is huge.

clue.text: Total, including present, getting stuck

indicators.note: to include something is to take it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to total is to add up
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: Adding up a sum including a gift and getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift, but it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adhered when it clung firmly to a surface, as glue does.

clue.text: Like father to come back without delay

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so letters run backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A parent's urgent request to return home immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like father' suggests 'like father, like son', but it is simply AS plus PA.
explanation.definitionFit: ASAP abbreviates 'as soon as possible', meaning at once, immediately.

clue.text: Dealt with mail hacker impeccably

indicators.note: dealt with means handled or worked over, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaking into emails was handled perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cyber-criminal being caught; the two middle words are just ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that works like a charm functions perfectly, flawlessly, as if by magic.

clue.text: Substantial contribution to molecular genetics

indicators.note: a contribution is a share of the whole, so the answer is a run of letters within the text

parts.note: letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A major scientific advance in the study of DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap: molecuLAR GEnetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and substantial both describe something of considerable size or amount.

clue.text: Allude one way or the other

indicators.note: it reads the same whichever direction you take it

parts.note: the definition supplies the word itself, and the indicator observes how it reads

explanation.surface: To hint at something, whichever side you take.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition supplies the word, and the rest of the clue observes that it reads identically top to bottom and bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to mention it indirectly, to make a passing mention of it.

clue.text: Great Tory leader slipped into prejudice

parts.note: big means great in size

indicators.note: a leader that has slipped has fallen from the front, so the order of letters changes

parts.note: taken as written; its leading letter is the one that moves

explanation.surface: A senior Conservative figure fell into intolerant views.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the head of TORY slips down one place to give OTRY. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant prejudice against people of other views, races or groups.

clue.text: Shore drift contents end in nasty shock

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters are discarded

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Material washed up on the beach has an unpleasant surprise inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shore drift' reads as a geographical term, but each word is gutted separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify is to fill someone with fear or disgust, to appal them.

clue.text: Sex with a tiny drop of dressing in green salad

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it
a salad is a mixture tossed together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: a tiny drop is the smallest amount, just the first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe: a green salad with just a splash of vinaigrette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green salad' looks like a dish, but 'salad' tells you to mix GREEN, and the first letter of dressing goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex and gender both name the category of male or female.

clue.text: Next door starting to get into beer for a heavy boozing session

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starting means at the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: The neighbours are starting on the beer for a big night of drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next door' looks like the neighbours, but only the initials of the two words go inside BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is a slang term for a drinking spree, a prolonged binge.
